s:
Arrange the following wheat-producing states in descending order of production:
A. Haryana
B. Madhya Pradesh
C. Uttar Pradesh
D. Punjab
x: The stated order is Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab and Haryana.

s: Wheat in India is chiefly associated with which group of States?
o: Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Madhya Pradesh
x: Wheat is chiefly grown in UP, Punjab, Haryana and MP; rice is grown with both rainfall and irrigation in many States.

s: Which States are listed as the leading maize producers of India?
x: Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh are listed as leading maize producers, with production rising in AP's Godavari–Krishna districts.

s: Which State is India's leading producer of bajra?
x: Bajra production order is Rajasthan > UP > Haryana.

s: Which State is the leading producer of ragi in India?
x: Karnataka leads in ragi.

s: In 2024-25, which State ranked second in rice production in India?
x: The 2024-25 order was UP (20.76 MT) > Telangana (17.45) > West Bengal (16.02) > Punjab (14.36).

s: Which State was the largest producer of rice in India in 2024-25?
x: In 2024-25 Uttar Pradesh led (20.76 MT), ahead of Telangana, West Bengal (16.02 MT) and Punjab; West Bengal is traditionally called the 'Rice Bowl of India'.

s: Which of the following States is a leading producer of jowar in India?
x: Jowar is a peninsular semi-arid crop led by Maharashtra and Karnataka.

s: Which State is the largest producer of pulses in India?
x: Madhya Pradesh is the largest pulse producer, followed by Rajasthan and Maharashtra.

s: Which is the principal food grain crop of Andhra Pradesh by production?
x: Of AP's 161.86 lakh MT of food grains in 2024-25, paddy alone was 127.15 lakh MT.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's foodgrain production in 2024-25?
x: AP produced 161.86 lakh MT of foodgrains (paddy 127.15 lakh MT) on 37.51 lakh ha in 2024-25.

s: What is the cause of ear cockle of wheat?
x: Ear cockle of wheat is caused by the nematode Anguina tritici. Colletotrichum causes red rot and Pyrilla is a sugarcane insect.

s: What causes black rust of wheat?
x: Black rust is caused by Puccinia graminis tritici; Ustilago causes loose smut, Sphaerulina narrow brown leaf spot and RTSV/RTBV rice tungro.

s: Tungro disease of rice is caused by which of the following?
x: Rice tungro is caused by the viruses RTSV and RTBV; Khaira is due to zinc deficiency.

s: Karnal bunt is a disease of which crop?
x: Karnal bunt of wheat is caused by Tilletia indica.

s: What are aflatoxins?
o: Toxins from moulds in badly stored grain
x: Aflatoxins come from moulds in badly stored grain and are not destroyed by cooking.

s: White bud of maize is caused by deficiency of which nutrient?
x: White bud of maize, like Khaira of rice, is caused by zinc deficiency.

s: Which of the following pairs (crop – growing condition) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Wheat – hot summer of the Zaid season
Rice – high temperature and rainfall above 100 cm
Cotton – black soil and frost-free conditions
Watermelon – hot summer of the Zaid season
x: Wheat needs a cool growing season with relatively dry conditions; the hot Zaid summer suits watermelon.

s: Which of the following combinations regarding wheat cultivation is correct?
o: Zaid crop; hot nights and waterlogged soils
Perennial crop; uniform rainfall throughout the year
Rabi crop; cool growing season, 50–75 cm rainfall and warm sunny ripening
Kharif crop; very high humidity and rainfall above 150 cm
x: Wheat is a rabi crop requiring a cool growing season, about 50–75 cm rainfall and warm, sunny conditions during ripening.

s: Rice is especially suited to which of the following soil and geographical environments?
o: Clayey or loamy soils of deltaic and coastal alluvial areas
Laterite soils of upland plateaus only
x: Rice is well suited to clayey or loamy soils, particularly the deltaic and coastal alluvium.

s: Pulses are used in crop rotation because they:
x: Pulses are leguminous and fix atmospheric nitrogen, so they are used in rotation.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Maize — Tamil Nadu; exclusively winter cultivation
Bajra — Rajasthan; driest conditions and sandy soils
Jowar — West Bengal; humid deltaic conditions
x: Rajasthan is the leading bajra-producing state, and bajra is suited to the driest conditions and sandy soils. Ragi is led by Karnataka, while jowar is associated mainly with Maharashtra and Karnataka.

s: Which isohyet marks the approximate western limit of rice cultivation in India?
x: The 100 cm isohyet marks the western limit of rice; Uttar Pradesh had the largest rice area in 2024–25.

s: What is the rank of wheat, mainly a rabi crop, among the cereals of India?
x: Wheat is India's second most important cereal; it is grown in the Ganga-Satluj plains and also the black-soil region of the Deccan.

s: Where is jowar grown mainly?
x: Jowar is grown mainly in peninsular and semi-arid India, led by Maharashtra and Karnataka. The Ganges delta grows rice and jute, the northern plains wheat, and humid coastal Kerala plantation crops.

s:
Consider the following statements about wheat in India:
1. It needs bright, warm sunshine at ripening.
2. The black soil of the Deccan is not suitable for wheat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Wheat needs bright warm sun at ripening. Statement 2 is wrong: wheat grows on the black soil of the Deccan as well as on Ganga-Satluj alluvium.

s: Which millet is a drought-tolerant crop of hot, dry conditions, led by Rajasthan?
x: Bajra suits hot, dry conditions on sandy soils and is led by Rajasthan; ragi is grown in peninsular India, especially Karnataka.

s: Where did rice originate?
x: Rice originated in South-East Asia.

s: Which of the following is NOT a stimulant crop?
x: Stimulant crops include tea, coffee, tobacco, opium poppy and betel nut; jute is a fibre crop.

s: What was India's record foodgrain production in 2024-25?
x: Foodgrain output was 357.73 MT in 2024–25, while horticulture was higher at 367.72 MT.

s: India, the largest rice exporter, accounts for about what share of world rice trade?
x: India has about 40 per cent of world rice trade; its rice output (150.18 MT) has also surpassed China's.

s: What was India's net sown area in 2021-22?
x: Net sown area was 141 MH and gross cropped area 219.16 MH in 2021-22.

s: Approximately what percentage of India's net sown area is irrigated?
x: Only 56.4 per cent of India's net sown area is irrigated.

s: Of which of the following is India the world's largest producer?
x: India is identified as the world's largest producer of pulses and millets.

s: Approximately what proportion of India’s irrigated area uses drip or sprinkler irrigation?
x: Only about 12% of the irrigated area is reported to use drip or sprinkler irrigation.

s: Which of the following is NOT among the world's top potato producers?
x: Brazil is not a top potato producer; production runs China > India > Russia, with Ukraine also major.

s: The USA Corn Belt is a classic region of which crop?
x: Maize grows in temperate and subtropical regions, the US Corn Belt being classic; wheat grows on the temperate grasslands.

s: Which country is the world's leading producer of maize?
x: Maize runs USA > China > Brazil; wheat runs China > India > Russia.

s: What was India's cropping intensity in 2021-22?
x: India's cropping intensity was 155.4% in 2021-22, reflecting a gross cropped area well above the net sown area. 121% and 188% resemble Andhra Pradesh's figures (1.21 in 2023-24, 1.88 in 2024-25), and 100% would mean no multiple cropping.

s: After which country does India have the world's second-largest arable land?
x: India's arable land is second only to the USA and is more than China's.

s: Since which year has India been the world's largest rice exporter?
x: India has been the largest rice exporter since 2014-15, with about 40% of world trade.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about irrigation in India?
o: India has the world's largest irrigated area
Wells and tube wells provide over 63% of irrigation
About 60% of agricultural land is irrigated
Drip and sprinkler cover only about 12% of irrigated area
x: Only about 56.4% of net sown area is irrigated, so 'about 60% irrigated' is incorrect.

s: Which country did India overtake in January 2026 to become the world's largest rice producer?
x: India's rice output of 150.18 MT passed China's 145.28 MT.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India is the world's largest rice exporter.
2. India is the world's largest wheat producer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India has been the largest rice exporter since 2014-15, but in wheat it is 2nd after China.

s: India accounts for about what share of the world's millet output?
x: India produces 18.59 MT of millets, about 42.75% of world output.

s: What is India's position in world wheat production?
x: India is 2nd in wheat after China, ahead of Russia.

s: Which country is the world's largest producer of wheat?
x: China leads wheat output, followed by India and Russia.

s: India is the world's largest producer and consumer of which of the following?
x: India is the world's largest producer and consumer of pulses and usually imports them.

s:
Consider the following statements about pulses in India:
1. India is the world's largest producer of pulses.
2. India is usually a large exporter of pulses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India is the largest producer and consumer of pulses but imports them because of high demand.

s: Which crop–season pair is correctly matched?
x: Watermelon is a zaid crop of the summer between rabi and kharif; rice is kharif and gram is rabi.

s: Which of the following is a Zaid crop?
x: Bitter gourd is zaid; peas and linseed are rabi and soybean is kharif.

s: Which of the following is NOT a Rabi crop?
x: Cucumber is a zaid crop; gram, mustard and lathyrus are rabi crops.

s: Which of the following pulses is a kharif crop?
x: Moong is a kharif pulse; gram, masoor and peas are rabi crops.

s: In which months is Aman rice, sown in June-July, harvested?
x: Aman rice is sown in June-July and harvested in November-December.

s: Which crop–season pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Watermelon is a zaid crop grown in the hot summer, not a rabi crop.

s: What type of crop is gram?
x: Gram is a rabi pulse; moong is a kharif pulse, cotton a kharif fibre crop and cucumber a zaid crop.

s: Which cereal is called the 'Queen of Cereals'?
x: Maize is called the Queen of Cereals and is grown throughout the year.

s: Procurement in India is criticised for being confined mainly to which crops, which use over two-thirds of India's urea?
x: Procurement is concentrated on rice, wheat and sugarcane, which together account for more than two-thirds of India's urea use.

s: On which crop was the first phase of the Green Revolution (mid-1960s to 1980s) largely centred?
x: Wheat was central to the first phase; rice benefited in a later, wider phase while pulses and coarse cereals lagged.

s: Which factors have been identified as favouring rice–wheat cultivation, including paddy in Punjab?
o: Minimum Support Price and free power
x: MSP arrangements and free power give rice and wheat policy advantages, favouring paddy in Punjab.

s: What is the N:P:K fertiliser-use ratio cited for Indian agriculture, compared with the ideal ratio?
x: The prevailing N:P:K ratio is cited as 10.9:4.1:1, whereas the ideal ratio is 4:2:1.

s: In which year did the New Agricultural Strategy associated with the Green Revolution in India begin?
x: The New Agricultural Strategy began in 1965 and combined HYV seeds, fertilisers, irrigation and minimum support price with the objective of foodgrain self-sufficiency.

s:
Consider the following statements about the limitations of the Green Revolution in India:
1. It led to groundwater depletion and salinity.
2. Pulses, oilseeds and millets were neglected.
3. Its gains were equally distributed among all landholders.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Groundwater depletion, salinity and the neglect of pulses, oilseeds and millets were recognised limitations. Statement 3 is wrong: big landowners benefited most.

s: Under which programme did India import wheat before the Green Revolution made it self-sufficient?
x: India moved from PL-480 wheat imports towards self-sufficiency, though rainfed and hill areas remained neglected.

s: In 1970, in which field did Norman Borlaug, who developed Mexican dwarf wheat, receive the Nobel Prize?
x: Borlaug received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970; M.S. Swaminathan is the father of India's Green Revolution and C. Subramaniam was the Union Agriculture Minister who backed it.

s: The Green Revolution in India mainly increased the production of which crops?
x: Wheat (first phase) and rice (later, wider phase) gained most, as in the APPSC 2025 key. Pulses, oilseeds and coarse cereals lagged; cotton and sugarcane were not the focus of the strategy.

s: What is Swaminathan's proposed remedy for the ecological limitations of the Green Revolution called?
x: The Evergreen Revolution was proposed as a sustainable corrective approach associated with M.S. Swaminathan.

s: Who coined the term 'Green Revolution' in 1968?
x: William Gaud coined the term in 1968.

s: Which Union Agriculture Minister backed the Green Revolution in India?
x: C. Subramaniam was the Union Agriculture Minister who backed it; B.P. Pal was the first DG of ICAR.

s: In its first stage, in which States did the Green Revolution mainly spread?
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
x: The first stage covered Punjab, Haryana and western UP; the eastern belt lagged.

s: Who was the first Director-General of ICAR?
x: B.P. Pal was the first Director-General of ICAR.

s: Who is known as the Father of the Green Revolution in India?
x: M.S. Swaminathan is the father in India; Borlaug is the father in the world.

s: From which season did the High Yielding Varieties Programme begin in India?
x: The HYV Programme began in Kharif 1966, after the New Agricultural Strategy of 1965.

s: As per 2015-16 data, what share of India's farmers are small and marginal farmers?
x: Small and marginal farmers are 86.2% of farmers but hold only 47.3% of the area.

s: Lerma Rojo 64-A and Sonora-64 used in India's Green Revolution are varieties of which crop?
x: Lerma Rojo 64-A, Sonora-63, Sonora-64 and Mayo-64 were Mexican dwarf wheat varieties.

s: Which is the dominant cropping system of the Indo-Gangetic Plains?
x: Rice-wheat is the dominant cropping system of the Indo-Gangetic Plains, with paddy followed by wheat as double cropping.

s: Which one of the following examples represents parallel cropping?
o: Tur and jowar sown together in definite rows
Maize and green gram grown together without competition
The next crop sown into a standing crop before its harvest
Paddy followed by wheat in the same year
x: Parallel cropping involves two crops of different growth habit and duration growing without competition; maize plus green gram is the stated example.

s: Towards which crops is agriculture in Andhra Pradesh diversifying from food grains?
o: fruits, vegetables, spices and oil palm
x: AP is diversifying from food grains towards fruits, vegetables, spices and oil palm.

s: What is intercropping?
o: Growing a crop only on fallow land
Sowing the next crop after complete removal of the previous crop
Growing one crop continuously for several years
Growing two or more crops together in definite rows
x: Intercropping involves growing two or more crops together in definite rows, such as tur with jowar or maize.

s: What is sowing the next crop into the standing crop before it is harvested called?
x: Relay cropping sows the next crop into the standing crop; ratoon cropping is regrowth from stubble and mixed cropping sows crops together without a row pattern.

s: What is growing a crop from the regrowth of the stubble of the previous crop called?
x: Ratoon is regrowth from stubble; relay cropping sows the next crop into the standing crop.

s:
Consider the following statements about cropping systems:
1. In intercropping, crops are grown together in definite rows.
2. In mixed cropping, seeds are mixed and sown with no row pattern.
3. Maize with green gram is an example of relay cropping.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Intercropping uses rows and mixed cropping has no row pattern. Maize with green gram is parallel cropping, not relay cropping.

s: To what level did the cropping intensity of Andhra Pradesh rise in 2024-25?
x: AP's cropping intensity rose from 1.21 (2023-24) to 1.88 (2024-25).

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Trans-Gangetic Plains — wheat and rice; highest productivity
Upper Gangetic Plains — plantations and jhum
Lower Gangetic Plains — wheat and rice; highest productivity
Eastern Himalayan Region — rice and jute as the principal pair
x: The Trans-Gangetic Plains include Punjab, Haryana and Delhi and are associated with wheat, rice and the highest productivity. The Upper Gangetic Plains are the core Green Revolution belt, the Lower Gangetic Plains are associated with rice and jute, and the Eastern Himalayan Region with plantations and jhum.

s: Which among the following agro-climatic regions is the core Green Revolution belt?
x: The Upper Gangetic Plains, particularly western Uttar Pradesh, constitute the core Green Revolution belt.

s:
Assertion (A): ICRISAT is located in Hyderabad, Telangana.
Reason (R): ICRISAT stands for International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: ICRISAT, the International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics, is at Patancheru near Hyderabad, but its full name does not explain why it is there.

s: Which of the following ICAR institutes is NOT correctly matched with its location?
o: Indian Institute of Pulses Research – Lucknow
Indian Institute of Rice Research – Hyderabad
Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research – Pedavegi (Eluru)
Indian Institute of Millets Research – Hyderabad
x: The Indian Institute of Pulses Research (former DPR) is at Kanpur, not Lucknow.

s: Where was the Directorate of Wheat Research located?
x: Wheat Research was at Karnal, Rice Research at Hyderabad, Maize Research at New Delhi and Pulses Research at Kanpur.

s: How many agro-climatic zones did the Planning Commission identify in the Seventh Plan?
x: There are 15 agro-climatic zones based on soil, climate and cropping pattern, sub-divided into 72 sub-zones.

s: Which body identified 20 agro-ecological zones in India?
x: The 20 agro-ecological zones are the work of the National Bureau of Soil Survey; the Planning Commission drew 15 agro-climatic zones.

s: Who proposed the four macro agricultural regions of India?
x: Sengupta and Sdasyuk divided India into four macro agricultural regions.

s: The 15 agro-climatic zones of the Planning Commission (Seventh Plan) are divided into how many sub-zones?
x: The Seventh Plan scheme has 15 agro-climatic zones and 72 sub-zones.

s: Where is the National Rice Research Institute (NRRI) located?
x: NRRI is at Cuttack; the Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) is at Hyderabad.

s: Which agro-climatic region, covering Punjab, Haryana and Delhi, has the highest agricultural productivity?
x: The Trans-Gangetic region (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi) grows wheat and rice and has the highest productivity.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pulses — high-moisture crop requiring continuous heavy rainfall
Millets — mainly kharif crops suited to dryland and rainfed tracts
Wheat — crop of hot and humid monsoon season
Rice — crop requiring low-input dryland conditions
x: Millets are mostly kharif crops and are climate-resilient, low-input crops of dryland and rainfed tracts.

s: Which group of crops is predominantly produced in India's rainfed areas?
x: Rainfed areas, which constitute about 51 per cent of net sown area, produce most of India's millets, pulses and oilseeds.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: Bajra, jowar and ragi are major millets. Foxtail, little, kodo and proso are minor millets.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Kodo millet is also called kodon; ragi is finger millet and belongs to the major millet group.

s: Which millet contributes about 60 per cent of India's millet output?
x: Bajra (pearl millet) gives about 60 per cent of India's millet output; India produces 42.75 per cent of world millets.

s: Under which brand name are millets promoted in India?
x: India brands millets as Shree Anna.

s: Which year was observed as the UN International Year of Millets, pushed by India?
x: 2023 was the UN International Year of Millets, at India's initiative.

s: Which of the following is a minor millet?
x: Kodo (kodon) is a minor millet; bajra, jowar and ragi are the major millets.

s: What is the upper limit of annual rainfall for dryland farming in India?
x: Dryland farming is done where rainfall is below 75 cm and there is no assured irrigation.

s: The shifting cultivation system known as ‘Dipa’ is associated with which of the following regions?
o: The agency areas of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
x: Dipa is the local name for shifting cultivation in Bastar, Chhattisgarh. Podu is associated with the agency areas of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

s: Which of the following communities are associated with the practice of shifting cultivation in Andhra Pradesh?
x: In Andhra Pradesh, shifting cultivation is practised by the Konda Reddi, Koya and Savara communities. The practice involves slash-and-burn cultivation followed by movement to another site.

s: Which of the following pairs (local name of shifting cultivation – region) is correctly matched?
x: Podu is the shifting cultivation of Andhra Pradesh. Milpa belongs to Mexico (Bastar has Dipa), Kumari to the Western Ghats and Bewar to Madhya Pradesh.

s: Which South Indian State practises shifting cultivation (jhumming), locally called podu, in the tribal tracts of the Eastern Ghats?
x: As the APPSC 2025 key held, Andhra Pradesh practises shifting cultivation known as podu (or penda) in its Eastern Ghats agency areas. Kerala's form is called ponam, and the Western Ghats form (Kerala, Karnataka) is called kumari; Tamil Nadu is not listed.

s: Where is the shifting cultivation known as 'Masole' practised?
x: Masole is the shifting cultivation of Central Africa (Congo). Roca is practised in Brazil, Ladang in Indonesia and Malaysia, and Milpa in Mexico and Central America.

s: Where is shifting cultivation called 'Chena'?
x: Chena is used in Sri Lanka; milpa in Central America and Mexico, conuco in Venezuela and tavy in Madagascar.

s: Which shifting cultivation–region pair is correctly matched?
x: Ladang is practised in Malaysia and Indonesia; jhum is in north-east India, roca in Brazil and taungya in Myanmar.

s: What does 'Fazenda' refer to?
x: Fazenda is a Brazilian plantation, not shifting cultivation; Brazil's shifting cultivation is Roca.

s: In which State is 'Pamlou' the local name for shifting cultivation?
x: Pamlou is practised in Manipur; Odisha has Pondu and Kerala has Poonam.

s: What is shifting cultivation locally called in Kerala?
x: Poonam (Ponam) is Kerala's name; Podu is AP, Bewar is MP and Jhum is the North-East.

s: From Kharif 2026, the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana was reported to cover which additional or specifically recognised contingencies?
o: Only drought affecting wheat and maize
Cyclones affecting all crops without exception
x: From Kharif 2026, PMFBY coverage was reported to include wild-animal attacks and paddy inundation.

s: Under which scheme was BGREI (Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India) launched in 2010-11?
x: BGREI was launched under RKVY for the rice-based cropping system of the eastern States.

s: In which year was the National Food Security Mission (NFSM) for rice, wheat and pulses launched?
x: NFSM began in 2007-08; nutri-cereals were added in 2018-19.

s: In which year was NFSM renamed as the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM)?
x: NFSM was renamed the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission in 2024-25.

s: Which of the following is NOT included among the crops covered by NFSNM?
x: NFSNM covers rice, wheat, pulses, maize, barley, Shree Anna, cotton, jute and sugarcane. Oilseeds and oil palm were moved to the NMEO initiatives.

s: What level of production do the NMEO-Oilseeds and NMEO-Oil Palm initiatives aim at by 2030-31?
x: The two missions target about 70 million tonnes by 2030-31.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Dalhan Aatmanirbharta Mission:
1. It was announced in October 2025.
2. It provides 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor.
3. The procurement assurance is for four years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Announced in October 2025, the mission provides 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor for four years, so all three statements are correct.

s: In which year were nutri-cereals added to the National Food Security Mission?
x: Nutri-cereals were added in 2018-19; coarse cereals and commercial crops came in 2014-15.

s: Which cropping system is targeted under Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI)?
x: BGREI, started in 2010-11 under RKVY, aims to raise productivity of the rice-based system of eastern India.

s: Which of the following States is NOT covered under BGREI?
x: BGREI covers Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, eastern UP and West Bengal, not Punjab.

s: From Kharif 2026, the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana covers which of the following new risks?
x: From Kharif 2026 PMFBY covers losses from wild-animal attacks and paddy inundation.

s: Which of the following is a major cotton-producing State of India?
x: The major cotton States are Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, mainly in black-soil regions.

s: Which one of the following sets correctly associates agricultural products or regions with Andhra Pradesh?
o: Oil palm leadership, Araku coffee, and Guntur chillies and tobacco
Darjeeling tea, Assam jute, and Nilgiri rubber
Kashmir saffron, Kerala coffee, and Malwa tobacco
Bengal jute, Coorg tea, and Konkan oil palm
x: Andhra Pradesh is associated with leadership in oil palm and with Araku coffee, Guntur chillies and tobacco.

s: In 2024-25, which State led India in tobacco production?
About what share of India's cotton area is under Bt cotton?
x: Bt cotton covers over 90% of India's cotton area.

s: Which State led India in coconut production in 2024-25?
x: In 2024-25 Tamil Nadu (30.17%) was ahead of Kerala (27.08%).

s: Which State leads India in both area and production of sugarcane?
x: Uttar Pradesh leads in both sugarcane area and production. Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu follow it; they belong to the tropical belt, which has higher yields but a smaller area under cane.

s: Which State leads India in rapeseed-mustard production?
x: Rajasthan produces about 45-49% of rapeseed-mustard.

s: How many oilseeds are covered under the Minimum Support Price system?
x: Seven oilseeds are listed under MSP: groundnut, rapeseed-mustard, soybean, sesamum, sunflower, safflower and nigerseed.

s: With reference to oilseeds in India, which one of the following trends was reported for 2025–26?
o: Production increased, but area and productivity declined.
Area increased, but production and productivity declined.
Area, production and productivity all increased.
Only productivity increased, while area and production remained unchanged.
x: For 2025–26, the area under oilseeds, their production and their productivity all recorded an increase.

s: Which oilseed is grown in both kharif and rabi seasons?
x: Sunflower is grown in both seasons; mustard and linseed are rabi, groundnut kharif.

s: Which of the following is a kharif oilseed?
x: Sesamum is a kharif oilseed; linseed, safflower and rapeseed are rabi oilseeds.

s: Which crop is called 'vegetable meat'?
x: Soybean is called vegetable meat.

s: Which State leads India in oil palm area, production and productivity?
x: Andhra Pradesh leads oil palm on all three counts.

s: For how many agricultural commodities does the Government announce Minimum Support Prices?
x: MSP covers 23 commodities: 7 cereals, 5 pulses, 7 oilseeds and commercial crops.

s: Which of the following is NOT covered under the Minimum Support Price system?
x: Areca nut, coffee and turmeric are not MSP crops; barley, nigerseed and safflower are.

s: Which crop–feature pair is correctly matched?
x: Groundnut came to India from Brazil; cotton suits black soil, sugarcane suffers red rot and jute grows in the Ganges delta.

s: What is the nature of plantation crops such as tea, coffee, rubber and coconut?
x: Plantation crops need substantial labour and capital; colonial plantations were European-dominated and export-oriented.

s: What was the nature of colonial plantations of tea, coffee, rubber and indigo in India?
x: Colonial plantations were European-dominated and export-oriented.

s: Which of the following groups consists only of food crops?
x: Wheat, rice and jowar are food crops; cotton, jute, tobacco, sugarcane, groundnut and bananas are cash crops.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the cultivation of cotton?
o: It needs a temperature of about 21–37°C
It grows best on the laterite soil of the Western Ghats
Black or regur soil is particularly suitable for it
It is mainly a kharif crop
x: Cotton is suited to black (regur) soil, not laterite; laterite of the Western Ghats is linked to rubber. The other statements are correct.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about plantation crops in India?
o: Rubber grows on the alluvial flood plains of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta with 50-70 cm of rain
Tea needs about 20-30°C, 150-300 cm of rain and acidic, well-drained hill slopes
Coffee needs about 15-28°C, shade and 150-250 cm of rain
Coffee needs deep, humus-rich, well-drained soil
x: Rubber needs a hot humid climate (25-35°C) with heavy rainfall; it is not a crop of the delta flood plains with 50-70 cm rain.

s: With which combination is jute cultivation most closely associated?
o: Cool dry climate and black soils
Cold climate, acidic hill slopes and low rainfall
Semi-arid climate and deep sandy loam
Hot humid climate, heavy rainfall and alluvial flood plains
x: Jute requires a hot, humid climate, high rainfall and alluvial soils of flood plains, particularly in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta.

s: Which of the following is a relatively water-efficient crop alternative in Indian agriculture?
x: Millets, pulses and oilseeds are water-efficient; paddy in Punjab and sugarcane in Maharashtra reflect subsidy distortions.

s: Which crop is linked to the laterite soil of the Western Ghats?
x: Laterite soil is linked to rubber; jute grows on alluvial flood plains, and black soils suit cotton, chillies and tobacco.

s: Sugarcane is a long-duration crop of about how many months?
x: Sugarcane takes about 10-15 months, needs hot humid conditions and grows on alluvial or black soil.

s: Which one of the following combinations is correct?
o: Red chilli — hot and dry conditions — Rajasthan
Red chilli — warm climate — Andhra Pradesh
Red chilli — cool season — northern India
Red chilli — warm and humid climate — Ganges Delta
x: Red chilli needs a warm climate and is a major crop of Andhra Pradesh.

s:
Assertion (A): Soybean requires a warm growing season.
Reason (R): Soybean is a major oilseed crop.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: being an oilseed does not explain why soybean needs a warm season.

s: Which is a major jute-producing delta region of the world?
x: Jute grows in hot, humid deltas, which is why the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta leads.

s: Which of the following pairs (crop – requirement) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tea – equatorial climate with over 200 cm of rainfall
Sugarcane – hot and humid conditions, heavy rain or irrigation, fertile soil
Rubber – equatorial climate with over 200 cm of rainfall
x: Tea needs moderate temperature, high rainfall and well-drained slopes; the equatorial climate with over 200 cm rain is rubber's requirement.

s: Which crop–requirement pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Rice — High temperature, heavy rainfall or irrigation, clayey soil
Coffee — Mild temperature, shade, well-drained slopes
Wheat — Cool growing season, bright sunshine at ripening
Rubber — Equatorial climate with about 100 cm rainfall
x: Rubber needs an equatorial climate with over 200 cm of rain, not 100 cm.

s: Rubber requires an annual rainfall of more than how much?
x: Rubber needs over 200 cm of rain, not 100 cm.

s: Which crops are grown mainly on black soils?
x: Black (regur) soils suit cotton, chillies and tobacco.

s: Which crop–leading producers pair is correctly matched?
x: China and India lead in tea; China, India and the USA lead in cotton, Brazil and Vietnam in coffee, and Thailand, Indonesia and Vietnam in rubber.

s: Which country is the world's leading producer of jute?
x: India is the leading jute producer, followed by Bangladesh.

s: Which country is the world's largest producer of tea?
x: China leads world tea output; India is 2nd.

s: What is India's rank in world natural rubber production (FAO 2024)?
x: India is 6th (5th earlier); Thailand leads.

s: What is India's rank in world coffee production?
x: India is 7th; Brazil and Vietnam lead.

s: Giza cotton, an extra-long staple variety, belongs to which country?
x: Giza is Egypt's extra-long staple cotton of the Nile valley; the USA grows Pima.

s: Which type of cotton does India mostly grow?
x: India grows mostly medium-staple cotton; extra-long staple comes mainly from Egypt.

s: Which country is the world's largest producer of cotton, with India second?
x: China leads cotton output, then India and the USA.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Coffee — Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu
Rubber — Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
x: Saffron is associated with Jammu and Kashmir, not Kerala. Kerala is a leading state for spices and rubber.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about cash crops in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Chilli and tobacco are grown in the black-soil belt
Guntur is a major chilli-trade hub
The Tobacco Board is headquartered at Guntur
AP ranks first in turmeric and second in chilli
x: The ranks are reversed: AP ranks first in chilli and second in turmeric.

s: To which State does Lakadong, a high-curcumin turmeric variety, belong?
x: Lakadong turmeric is from Meghalaya, which also leads in pineapple; Arunachal grows over half of India's kiwi.

s: In the production of which crop does Andhra Pradesh rank first in India?
x: AP is 1st in chillies and 2nd in turmeric; Gujarat now leads tobacco.

s: Which town of Andhra Pradesh is the chilli-trade hub and seat of the Tobacco Board?
x: Guntur is the chilli-trade hub and the seat of the Tobacco Board.

s: Which State led India in spices production in 2024-25?
x: Madhya Pradesh led spice output in 2024-25, though Kerala is famous as the Spice Garden.

s: Which State is the leading producer of clove in India?
x: Tamil Nadu leads clove production in India.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Rubber Board?
x: The Rubber Board is at Kottayam, the Coffee Board at Bengaluru, the Tea Board at Kolkata and the Spices Board at Kochi.

s: Under which Ministry does the Coconut Development Board (Kochi) function?
x: It is under the Ministry of Agriculture; the Tea, Coffee, Rubber, Spices and Tobacco Boards are under the Department of Commerce.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Spices Board?
x: The Spices Board is at Kochi; the Rubber Board is at Kottayam.

s: Which commodity board has its headquarters in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Tobacco Board is at Guntur, the only board seated in AP.

s: How many statutory commodity boards function under the Ministry of Commerce?
x: Five statutory boards are under Commerce: tea, coffee, rubber, spices and tobacco.

s: Where is the headquarters of the National Jute Board?
x: The National Jute Board, under the Ministry of Textiles, is at Kolkata.

s: Where is the headquarters of the National Turmeric Board?
x: The National Turmeric Board, launched in January 2025 under the Commerce Ministry, has its headquarters at Nizamabad, Telangana.

s: Which of the following pairs (board – headquarters) is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Coffee Board is at Bengaluru; Kottayam is the Rubber Board's seat. Turmeric Board is at Nizamabad.

s: Where is the Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI) located?
x: CPCRI is at Kasaragod.

s: Where is the Indian Institute of Spices Research located?
x: IISR (spices) is at Kozhikode; the other IISR (sugarcane) is at Lucknow.

s: Where is the Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres (CRIJAF) located?
x: CRIJAF is at Barrackpore; the Natural Fibre Engineering institute is at Kolkata.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Institute)
a. Central Potato Research Institute
b. Temperate Horticulture Institute
c. Tuber Crops Research Institute
d. Dr. Y.S. Parmar University
List-II (Location)
1. Thiruvananthapuram
2. Solan
3. Shimla
4. Srinagar
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Potato research is at Shimla, temperate horticulture at Srinagar, tuber crops at Thiruvananthapuram and Dr. Y.S. Parmar University at Solan.

s: The Araku coffee cluster is located in which State?
x: Araku and the ASR district are AP's coffee clusters; Kodagu is in Karnataka and the Nilgiris in Tamil Nadu.

s: With which hills is Arabica coffee in India particularly associated?
x: Arabica coffee is associated with the Baba Budan Hills in Chikkamagaluru, Karnataka. The two principal coffee varieties mentioned are Arabica and Robusta.

s: What distinction does Darjeeling Tea have in India?
x: Darjeeling Tea was India’s first product to receive a Geographical Indication tag.

s: The Dooars region is known for which plantation crop?
x: Darjeeling and the Dooars in West Bengal are tea areas.

s: When were the first tea plantations started in the Brahmaputra valley of Assam?
x: India's first tea plantations came up in the Brahmaputra valley in the first half of the 19th century.

s: In which State were the first tea plantations of India set up?
x: Tea plantations began first in the Brahmaputra valley of Assam.

s: Where was tea first grown in Africa, in 1850?
x: Tea in Africa was first grown at the Durban Botanical Garden in 1850; it later spread to Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

s: Sugar mills are located near the cane fields because sugarcane is a:
x: Cane loses weight and sugar after cutting, so mills are located near the fields.

s: During which months does the sugarcane crushing season run in the tropical belt of India?
x: The tropical crushing season is longer, October to May/June; November to February is the sub-tropical season.

s: Which of the following pairs (sugarcane belt – favourable factor) is correctly matched?
o: Uttar Pradesh–Bihar – Predominance of shifting cultivation
Uttar Pradesh–Bihar – Scarcity of alluvial soil
Uttar Pradesh–Bihar – Fertile alluvium rich in lime and potash
x: The northern sugarcane concentration rests on fertile alluvium rich in lime and potash, level land, dense markets and compact cane blocks; western Uttar Pradesh is the main sugar-mill belt.

s: During which months does the sugarcane crushing season run in the sub-tropical belt of north India?
x: The sub-tropical crushing season is November to February; the tropical belt's is October to May/June.

s:
Consider the following statements about sugarcane in tropical south India:
1. Its yield is higher than in sub-tropical north India.
2. Cool nights with clear skies and long sunshine favour it.
3. Its crushing season is shorter than in the north.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Tropical cane yields more because of cool clear nights and long sunshine, and its crushing season (Oct to May/June) is longer.

s: What is the administered price for sugarcane in India?
x: Sugarcane is covered by the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP), not the Minimum Support Price.

s: To what does the Round Revolution relate?
x: The Round Revolution is potato; Black is petroleum, Pink is onion or meat and Brown is leather or non-conventional energy.

s: What does the Rainbow Revolution refer to?
o: integrated development of agriculture and allied sectors
x: The Rainbow Revolution combines the Green, White, Blue and other coloured revolutions for integrated growth of agriculture and allied sectors.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Yellow Revolution is about oilseeds; horticulture and honey belong to the Golden Revolution.

s: With which revolution is the Technology Mission on Cotton associated?
x: The Technology Mission on Cotton is associated with the Silver Fibre Revolution.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Golden Revolution is associated with horticulture and honey. Cotton is associated with the Silver Fibre Revolution, while jute is associated with the Golden Fibre and Golden Fibre Revolution.

s: Which fibre is called 'Golden Fibre'?
x: Jute is the Golden Fibre; cotton is the Silver Fibre.

s: To which crop does the Silver Fibre Revolution relate?
x: Silver Fibre is cotton, linked to the Technology Mission on Cotton.

s: To what is the Golden Revolution related?
x: The Golden Revolution is horticulture and honey; oilseeds are the Yellow Revolution.

s: With which of the following is the Brown Revolution associated?
x: Brown Revolution relates to leather (also non-conventional energy and fertiliser).

s: In which year was Operation Flood launched by the NDDB?
x: Operation Flood of the NDDB began in 1970; Verghese Kurien led the White Revolution.

s: From which country do Indian jute goods face export competition mainly?
x: Bangladesh competes with Indian jute goods in exports, while cotton competes with synthetic fibres.

s: At what price does the Jute Corporation of India purchase raw jute when market prices fall?
o: A price fixed by the National Horticulture Board
x: The Jute Corporation of India buys raw jute at the minimum support price when market prices fall.

s: The Paat-Mitro mobile application is associated with which crop?
x: Paat-Mitro was launched in 2023 for jute farmers.

s: What packing requirement is prescribed under the Jute Packaging Materials Act, 1987?
o: 50% of food grains and 50% of sugar in jute
100% of food grains and 20% of sugar in jute
100% of food grains and 100% of sugar in jute
20% of food grains and 100% of sugar in jute
x: The Act requires 100% of food grains and 20% of sugar to be packed in jute, subject to the stated provisions.

s: What is the full form of Jute-ICARE?
o: Integrated Crop and Agricultural Research Enterprise
Improved Cultivation and Advanced Retting Exercise
Improved Crop Assessment and Retting Evaluation
x: Jute-ICARE is Improved Cultivation and Advanced Retting Exercise, with certified seed and the SONA retting consortium.

s: Which State is stated to be India's largest fruit producer, with a share of about 15.6%?
x: Andhra Pradesh is stated to be India's largest fruit producer, accounting for about 15.6% of production.

s: India occupies which position in the world in fruit and vegetable production?
x: India is stated to be the second-largest producer in the world of fruits and vegetables.

s: What is the Centre-State funding ratio under MIDH for North-Eastern and Himalayan States?
x: MIDH funding is 60:40, and 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States; its sub-schemes include NHM, HMNEH and the National Bamboo Mission.

s: Which State produces over 50% of India's kiwi fruit?
x: Arunachal Pradesh produces over half of India's kiwi.

s: Which State is the leading producer of litchi in India?
x: Bihar leads in litchi; Meghalaya in pineapple.

s: Horticulture provides about what share of India's agricultural GDP?
x: Horticulture gives about 30.4% of agricultural GDP from under 14% of cropped area.

s: Which State is listed as the second-largest producer of raw silk in India?
x: Andhra Pradesh is listed as the second-largest producer of raw silk, after Karnataka.

s: Which silk variety is endemic to Assam and is produced by the silkworm Antheraea assamensis?
x: Muga silk is endemic to Assam and is produced by Antheraea assamensis.

s: Which silk–food plant pair is correctly matched?
x: Eri silkworms feed on castor and tapioca; Tropical Tasar on Terminalia and Sal, Muga on Som and Soalu, and Mulberry on mulberry.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Central Silk Board?
x: The headquarters of the Central Silk Board is at Bengaluru.

s: In the life cycle of a honey bee, which stage comes immediately after the larva?
x: Honey bees pass through egg, larva, pupa and adult, so the pupa follows the larva.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Apiculture is the rearing of bees and yields honey and bee-wax. Sericulture yields silk, pisciculture yields fish and floriculture concerns flowers.

s: On which plant do the silkworms of Eri silk, known as 'peace silk', feed?
x: Eri silkworms feed on castor (and tapioca); muga feeds on som and soalu.

s: On which plants do Muga silkworms feed?
x: Muga feeds on som and soalu; tasar feeds on Terminalia and sal.

s: In which State is oak (temperate) tasar silk mainly produced?
x: Oak tasar comes from Manipur, Uttarakhand, HP and J&K.

s: What is reared in lac culture?
x: Lac culture produces lac from lac insects.

s:
Consider the following statements about silk in India:
1. India is the only country producing all five silks.
2. India is the largest producer of raw silk in the world.
3. Karnataka is the largest silk-producing State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India produces all five silks and Karnataka leads. Statement 2 is wrong: India is 2nd after China.

s: In which districts of Andhra Pradesh is tasar silk mainly produced?
o: East Godavari and Alluri Sitarama Raju
x: AP's tasar silk comes from East Godavari and ASR (Rampachodavaram) districts.

s: What was India's horticulture output in 2024-25?
x: Horticulture output was 362.08 MT in 2024–25, above foodgrain output, giving about 33% of agricultural GVA from under 14% of cropped area.

s: Which Indian State is identified as the largest fruit-producing State, contributing approximately 15.6 per cent of India's national fruit output?
x: Andhra Pradesh is identified as India's largest fruit-producing State, with approximately 15.6 per cent of national fruit output.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Kinnaur temperate apple belt – Himachal Pradesh
Largest true potato seed producer – Tripura
Second in mango production – Andhra Pradesh
x: Lakadong turmeric comes from Meghalaya, not Tripura. The other three pairs are correct.

s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of crops introduced by the Portuguese into India?
o: Tea, coffee, rubber, jute and cotton
Cashew, tomato, chilli, potato and tobacco
Rice, wheat, gram, mustard and barley
Millet, maize, sugarcane, sesame and pulses
x: The Portuguese introduced cashew, tomato, chilli, potato and tobacco, among other crops, into India.

s: Which State is known as the 'Orchid State' of India?
x: Arunachal Pradesh has the most orchid species; Sikkim is 2nd.

s: Which State is India's largest mango producer?
x: Uttar Pradesh leads in mango; AP is 2nd.

s: Which State produces over 50% of India's kiwi?
x: Arunachal Pradesh grows over half of India's kiwi.

s: Which State now leads India in loose flower production?
x: Tamil Nadu, followed by West Bengal, now leads in loose flowers.

s: Horticulture contributes about what share of India's agricultural GVA?
x: Horticulture (362.08 MT in 2024-25) gives about 33% of agri GVA from under 14% of cropped area.

s: Which State is the leading producer of litchi in India?
x: Bihar is the leading litchi State.

s: What is the botanical name of pineapple?
x: Pineapple is Ananas comosus of the family Bromeliaceae.

s: In the productivity of which crop does Andhra Pradesh rank first in India?
x: AP is 1st in cocoa productivity.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Barbari is a goat breed of Uttar Pradesh, not a poultry breed. Hallikar, Murrah and Jamunapari are correctly matched.

s: Which breed–species–native region combination is correctly matched?
x: Ongole is a cattle breed native to the Prakasam district of Andhra Pradesh. Murrah is a buffalo, Kadaknath is poultry, and Jamunapari is a goat.

s: Punganur, a dwarf cattle breed, is native to which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Punganur is from Chittoor; Ongole is from Prakasam.

s: Of which animal is Murrah a breed?
x: Murrah is a buffalo breed of Haryana.

s: To which State is Kadaknath, a poultry breed with black meat, native?
x: Kadaknath comes from Jhabua, Madhya Pradesh.

s: The Jamunapari goat comes from which State?
x: Jamunapari is a goat of Etawah, Uttar Pradesh.

s: To which State does Hallikar, a draught cattle breed, belong?
x: Hallikar is a Karnataka draught breed.

s: What is Frieswal?
o: A goat breed of Uttar Pradesh
A poultry breed of Madhya Pradesh
x: Frieswal is a synthetic cattle breed giving about 7,000 kg of milk per lactation.

s: The Gir breed of cattle is native to which State?
x: Gir cattle come from the Gir forest of Gujarat.

s: Which of the following pairs (breed – native State) is correctly matched?
x: Kankrej is a Gujarat breed; Gir is Gujarat, Hallikar Karnataka and Tharparkar Rajasthan.

s: Bhadawari is a breed of which animal?
x: Bhadawari is a buffalo breed of the UP-MP region.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched (breed – species)?
x: Gir is a cattle breed of Gujarat; Murrah is buffalo, Barbari goat and Kadaknath poultry.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about types of fisheries?
o: Inland fisheries covers fresh water such as rivers, tanks and reservoirs
Marine fisheries covers coastal and deep-sea fishing
Capture fisheries means the controlled farming of fish, shrimp and molluscs
Inland fisheries also covers brackish water such as estuaries and lagoons
x: Capture fisheries harvests wild stock; controlled farming is not capture fishing. The other three are correct.

s: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) launched?
x: PMMSY was launched in 2020 by the Department of Fisheries, with the NFDB providing training; its Central Sector component is fully centrally funded. The other years are not its launch year.

s: What is the harvest of wild fish stock called?
x: Capture fishery harvests wild stock; culture (aquaculture, mariculture) is controlled farming.

s: Above what altitude are cold-water fisheries such as trout found?
x: Trout cold-water fisheries lie above 1,500 m.

s: Where is the Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture (CIFA) located?
x: CIFA is at Bhubaneswar; CIFT and CMFRI are at Kochi.

s: What is India's rank in world fish production?
x: India is the 2nd largest fish producer.

s: Where is the Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) located?
x: CMFRI and CIFT are at Kochi; CIFA is at Bhubaneswar.

s: In India, inland fisheries contribute more than what proportion of total fish output?
x: Inland fisheries contribute more than 75 percent of India’s total fish output.

s: Where is the Central Institute for Research on Cattle located?
x: The Central Institute for Research on Cattle is at Meerut, Uttar Pradesh. Bengaluru has the animal nutrition institute, Bhopal the high-security animal disease institute and Ranchi the agricultural biotechnology institute.

s: Where is the Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute located?
x: Sheep and wool research is at Avikanagar, Rajasthan.

s: Where is the High Security Animal Disease Laboratory located?
x: It is at Bhopal; Karnal hosts NDRI.

s: Where is ICRISAT located?
x: ICRISAT is at Patancheru, Hyderabad.

s: What was India's per capita milk availability in 2024-25?
x: It was 485 g/day in 2024-25, up from 471 g/day in 2023-24.

s: What was India's milk production during 2024-25?
x: India produced 247.87 million tonnes of milk in 2024–25 (239.30 MT in 2023–24; 146.31 MT in 2014–15).

s: What is the main aim of the Rashtriya Gokul Mission?
o: Development and conservation of indigenous bovine breeds
Promotion of sericulture in tribal areas
x: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission focuses on indigenous breeds; AP's Gokul Gram at Chadalawada (Prakasam) is a cattle-breeding farm under it. Building milk- and meat-processing capacity is the job of the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund; fish seed and sericulture belong to other schemes.

s: Which one of the following is described as the fastest-growing farm sub-sector, with approximately 8.8 per cent decadal growth?
x: Fisheries is described as the fastest-growing farm sub-sector, with approximately 8.8 per cent decadal growth. Livestock growth is stated as about 7.1 per cent.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the growth of livestock and fisheries during FY15–FY24?
o: Livestock GVA grew by about 195 percent
Livestock and fisheries grew at identical rates of 8.8 percent
Livestock grew at about 7.1 percent over the decade
Fisheries grew at about 8.8 percent over the decade
x: The rates were not identical: livestock grew about 7.1 percent and fisheries about 8.8 percent. Livestock GVA did grow about 195 percent.

s: As per the 20th Livestock Census, what was India's total livestock population?
x: Total livestock was 535.78 million, up 4.6% over 2012; 302.79 million were bovines.

s: In which year was the 20th Livestock Census of India conducted?
x: The 20th Census was in 2019; the 21st (2024-25) is digital.

s: Which body launched Operation Flood in 1970?
x: Operation Flood (1970) was run by the National Dairy Development Board.

s: What is the main aim of the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund?
x: AHIDF supports milk- and meat-processing capacity; Rashtriya Gokul Mission conserves indigenous breeds.

s: Which Livestock Census was conducted in 2024-25 with fully digital enumeration?
x: The 21st Livestock Census (2024-25) used digital enumeration; the 20th was in 2019.

s: With which revolution is Verghese Kurien associated?
x: Verghese Kurien is the Father of the White Revolution (milk), led through Operation Flood by NDDB.

s: To what is the Grey Revolution related?
x: The Grey Revolution relates to fertilisers.

s: To what is the Silver Revolution related?
x: Silver Revolution is eggs and poultry; Silver Fibre is cotton.

s: Which of the following pairs (revolution – sector) is correctly matched?
o: Pink Revolution – Onion and meat export
x: Pink is onion and meat export. Yellow is oilseeds, Golden is horticulture and Blue is fish.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Revolution)
A. Blue
B. Yellow
C. Golden
D. Grey
List-II (Sector)
1. Oilseeds
2. Fertilisers
3. Fish
4. Horticulture and honey
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Blue is fish, Yellow is oilseeds, Golden is horticulture and honey, Grey is fertilisers.

s: Andhra Pradesh is noted for which of the following combinations?
o: First in cocoa productivity and a growth-engine region for cashew
First in tea production and a major rubber region
Largest producer of arecanut and coffee
Exclusive producer of Muga silk and saffron
x: Andhra Pradesh is first in cocoa productivity, and cashew is identified as a Rayalaseema/Andhra Pradesh growth-engine crop.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes arecanut?
o: It is a rabi crop requiring a cool, dry climate.
It is a zaid crop grown in irrigated summer fields.
It is a fibre crop grown mainly in the Ganges Delta.
It is a plantation crop requiring a tropical humid climate.
x: Arecanut is a plantation crop that needs a tropical humid climate, grown mainly in Karnataka and Kerala. It is not a seasonal rabi or zaid crop, nor a fibre crop.

s: Which of the following plantation crops falls under the Ministry of Commerce?
x: Tea, coffee and rubber are under Commerce; coconut, arecanut, cashew, palm and cocoa under Agriculture.

s: India ranks first globally in dry onion production; in the production of which of the following did it also overtake China?
x: India is stated to rank first in dry onions and to have overtaken China in rice production.

s: What is India's rank in world vegetable production?
x: India is the second-largest producer of vegetables, not the first (a known APPSC trap); it is first in milk.

s: What is India's rank in world egg production?
x: India is 2nd in eggs, with 149.11 billion in 2024-25.

s: What was India's egg production in 2024-25?
x: India produced 149.11 billion eggs in 2024-25 and is 2nd in the world.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, with which districts are sugar mills mainly associated?
x: Agro-industries locate near raw materials; AP's sugar mills are associated with the Godavari districts, Visakhapatnam and Chittoor.

s: In which year was PMFME (PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises) launched under Aatmanirbhar Bharat?
x: PMFME was launched in 2020 under Aatmanirbhar Bharat on a One District One Product basis; 2017 is when PM Kisan SAMPADA was approved.

s: Processed food constituted approximately what share of India's agri-food exports in 2024–25?
x: Processed food accounted for about 23 percent of agri-food exports in 2024–25.

s: What kind of scheme is PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana, approved in 2017?
o: Central Sector scheme with an integrated cold-chain component
State Sector scheme excluding cold-chain infrastructure
x: PM Kisan SAMPADA was approved in 2017 as a Central Sector scheme and includes integrated cold chain among its components.

s: How many Mega Food Parks are operational in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP has 3 sanctioned Mega Food Parks, of which 2 are operational.

s: To which approach is PMFME (2020) linked?
x: PMFME, under Aatmanirbhar Bharat, follows One District One Product.

s: In which year was the APEDA Act passed?
x: The APEDA Act dates from 1985.

s: In which district of Andhra Pradesh is the Srini Mega Food Park located?
x: Srini Mega Food Park is in Chittoor; Godavari Mega Aqua Park is in West Godavari.

s: Which State ranks first in India in both egg production and aquaculture?
x: Andhra Pradesh is ranked first in egg production and in aquaculture.

s: Which State accounts for nearly 29% of India's fish production and leads in both fish and shrimp?
x: Andhra Pradesh contributes nearly 29% of India's fish production and leads in both fish and shrimp; India as a whole is the 2nd largest fish producer. West Bengal, Kerala and Gujarat are important fish States but none leads.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the coastline of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The earlier reported coastline length was 974 km
By the 2023–24 remeasurement, AP has the third-longest coastline
On the earlier measurement, AP was regarded as having the second-longest coastline
On the earlier measurement, AP was ranked third in coastline length
x: Earlier AP was regarded as having the second-longest coastline, not the third; it is third only after the 2023–24 remeasurement.

s: According to APSES 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh accounts for approximately what share of India’s total fish production?
x: Andhra Pradesh is estimated to contribute about 29% of India’s total fish production according to APSES 2025-26. The earlier estimate was about 30% in APSES 2024-25.

s: Shrimp accounts for nearly what share of Andhra Pradesh's seafood export basket?
x: Shrimp makes up about 70% of AP's seafood exports; 32% is AP's share of India's seafood exports (2022–23, 2023–24).

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's fish production in 2024-25?
x: AP produced 55.39 LMT of fish in 2024-25; 51.58 LMT was 2023-24 and 51.06 LMT was 2022-23.

s: After the 2023-24 remeasurement, what is the rank of Andhra Pradesh's 1,053 km coastline in India?
x: AP's coastline is now 1,053 km, the 3rd longest behind Gujarat and Tamil Nadu; earlier it was 974 km and 2nd.

s: Andhra Pradesh ranks first in India in which of the following?
x: AP ranks first in India in fish and shrimp production thanks to its long coastline and large aquaculture; tea is led by Assam, silk by Karnataka and jute by West Bengal.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh ranks first in India in fish and shrimp production.
2. After the 2023-24 remeasurement, Andhra Pradesh has the second-longest coastline in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AP is first in fish and shrimp production, but after the remeasurement its 1,053 km coastline is third, behind Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

s: In which year did Andhra Pradesh record the highest inland fish landings in India?
x: AP recorded the highest inland fish landings in India in 2019-20.

s: Andhra Pradesh accounts for about what share of India's seafood exports?
x: AP gives about 32% of India's seafood exports; 29% is its share of fish production and 70% is shrimp's share of AP's export basket.

s: What is the full form of IQF, the standard freezing method for seafood exports?
x: IQF means Individually Quick Frozen: each piece, such as a shrimp, is frozen separately and fast.

s: Which shrimp is the main export item of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Vannamei (white-leg) shrimp is the main export item; black tiger shrimp brood multiplication is done at the MPEDA centre at Visakhapatnam.

s: The AP Fisheries University was established under which Act and is located in which district?
o: AP Fisheries University Act, 2020 — West Godavari
x: The AP Fisheries University was established under the AP Fisheries University Act, 2020, and is located in West Godavari district.

s: What is the period of the uniform 61-day marine fishing ban on India's East Coast?
x: The East Coast ban runs for 61 days, from 15 April to 14 June.

s: During the fishing-ban period in Andhra Pradesh, which craft are exempt from the ban?
o: Motorised boats operating within 12 nautical miles
x: Traditional non-motorised craft are exempt. Mechanised and motorised boats are banned in territorial waters during the specified period.

s: What is the front-end HSD diesel subsidy provided for fishing boats in Andhra Pradesh during 2025–26?
x: The front-end HSD subsidy was ₹9 per litre.

s:
Consider the following statements about AP's fishing-ban relief for marine fishermen families:
1. YSR Matsyakara Bharosa raised the relief from Rs 4,000 to Rs 10,000 from 2019-20.
2. The relief was raised to Rs 20,000 per family from 2024-25.
3. The scheme was renamed Matsyakara Sevalo in 2019-20.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Relief rose to Rs 10,000 from 2019-20 and Rs 20,000 from 2024-25; the renaming as Matsyakara Sevalo came in 2025-26, not 2019-20.

s: How much ban-period relief per family is given to marine fishermen in Andhra Pradesh from 2024-25?
x: The fishing-ban relief rose from ₹4,000 to ₹10,000 in 2019-20 and to ₹20,000 per family from 2024-25.

s: About what share of Andhra Pradesh's foodgrain output comes from paddy?
x: Paddy gives about 79% of AP's foodgrain output, though it occupies only about 56% of the foodgrain area.

s: Which of the following is NOT included among the crops identified under the 17 growth engines for raising productivity?
x: The 17 growth engines cover 11 crops including paddy, maize, jowar, bajra, ragi, pulses, groundnut, sunflower and sesamum. Coffee is not in this list.

s: Towards which crops is the cropping pattern of Andhra Pradesh recently shifting?
o: Oilseeds, millets, horticulture and oil palm
x: AP's cropping pattern is shifting towards oilseeds, millets, horticulture and oil palm, with productivity initiatives for 11 crops.

s: Which of the following pairs about Andhra Pradesh's Kharif 2026 season is correctly matched?
x: AP faced a 51 percent rainfall shortfall from 1 June to 25 August 2026 under El Niño conditions, so it proposed a water-budgeted shift towards pulses in Kharif 2026.

s: What is the target of the Andhra Pradesh agricultural growth strategy?
o: 30 percent growth in horticulture over five years through 21 growth engines
48.3 percent growth in agriculture over five years through 17 growth engines
30 percent growth in agriculture over five years through 17 growth engines
21 percent growth in agriculture over three years through 12 growth engines
x: The strategy targets 30 percent growth in agriculture over five years and identifies 17 growth engines.

s: Which of the following is identified as one reason for the shrinkage of coarse cereal cultivation in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Lack of minimum support price procurement
Excessive canal irrigation in every district
x: Coarse cereal cultivation has been shrinking partly because of inadequate MSP procurement.

s: The cropping intensity of 1.88 in Andhra Pradesh relates to which year?
x: Cropping intensity was 1.88 in 2024-25; it was 1.21 in 2023-24.

s: Which is the main crop season of Andhra Pradesh by normal cropped area?
x: Kharif normal area is about 31.16 lakh ha (2025), larger than the Rabi normal of 21.52 lakh ha (2024-25).

s: What was the normal area of the Rabi 2024-25 season in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Commissionerate of Agriculture put the Rabi 2024-25 normal area at 21.52 lakh ha.

s: Which district is known as the Rice Bowl of Andhra Pradesh?
x: East Godavari is known as the Rice Bowl of Andhra Pradesh. Its delta rice cultivation is supported by canal irrigation.

s: Which crop of Andhra Pradesh is associated with the black soils of Rayalaseema and the districts of Guntur and Kurnool?
x: Cotton is grown on Rayalaseema's black soils and in Guntur and Kurnool; chillies are prominent in Guntur–Krishna, maize in Godavari–Krishna and banana in Rayalaseema clusters.

s: In the red soils of Rayalaseema, which crop can be grown only with irrigation?
x: Red soils support groundnut, ragi and tobacco, while rice and sugarcane need irrigation in them.

s: Which of the following crop – principal region pairs of Andhra Pradesh is wrongly matched?
o: Paddy – East Godavari and the Godavari–Krishna deltas
x: Tobacco is concentrated in Prakasam and Guntur; the ASR–Araku region is the coffee area.

s: Tobacco in Andhra Pradesh is mainly grown in which districts?
x: Tobacco is a crop of Prakasam and Guntur; ASR (Araku) is the coffee area.

s: The Araku area of ASR district is known for which crop?
x: ASR (Araku) is the coffee area of AP, not a tobacco area.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh is the leading area for chillies?
x: Chillies in Andhra Pradesh are grown mainly in Guntur, along with Krishna.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Crop)
a. Chillies
b. Groundnut
c. Coffee
d. Tobacco
List-II (Area)
I. Araku (ASR)
II. Prakasam
III. Anantapur
IV. Guntur
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Chillies – Guntur, groundnut – Anantapur, coffee – Araku (ASR) and tobacco – Prakasam.

s: Where is the Gokul Gram cattle-breeding farm of Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The AP Gokul Gram cattle-breeding farm is at Chadalawada in Prakasam district.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank in milk production in 2025-26?
x: AP was 7th in milk, 4th in meat and 1st in eggs.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank in meat production in 2025-26?
x: AP was 4th in meat (5th in 2023-24).

s: Which is Andhra Pradesh's leading milk-producing district?
x: Chittoor is AP's leading dairy district.

s: Where is the National Kamadhenu Breeding Centre of Andhra Pradesh, set up under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission, located?
x: The National Kamadhenu Breeding Centre is at Chintaladeevi; Chadalawada has the Gokul Gram.

s: Which breed–livestock pair is correctly matched?
x: Godavari is a buffalo type; Ongole and Punganur are cattle breeds and Nellore is a sheep breed.

s: Where is AP's Gokul Gram cattle breeding farm under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission?
x: The Gokul Gram farm is at Chadalawada, Prakasam; Chintaladevi in Nellore hosts the National Kamdhenu Breeding Centre.

s: Where is the National Kamdhenu Breeding Centre in Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The National Kamdhenu Breeding Centre is at Chintaladevi in Nellore district.

s:
Consider the following statements about native livestock breeds of Andhra Pradesh:
1. Punganur is a cattle breed.
2. Nellore is a sheep breed.
3. Aseel is a buffalo breed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Ongole and Punganur are cattle, Nellore is sheep; Aseel is a poultry breed and Godavari the buffalo breed.

s: Small and marginal farmers holding up to 2 hectares constitute approximately what share of India's farmers?
x: Farmers with holdings of up to 2 hectares constitute approximately 86.2% of India's farmers.

s: What was the average size of land holding in Andhra Pradesh as per the Agriculture Census 2015-16?
x: The Agriculture Census 2015-16 gives an average holding of 0.94 ha for AP against 1.08 ha for India.

s: Under Andhra Pradesh's inland fisheries strategy, to whom are departmental tanks leased?
x: Departmental tanks are leased to fishermen cooperative societies, alongside fish seed stocking and reservoir and tank fisheries.

s: Which group of districts is identified as the shrimp backbone of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Prakasam, West Godavari, East Godavari, Nellore and Krishna
Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli and Bapatla
Guntur, Anantapur, Kurnool, Nellore and Srikakulam
Eluru, Kakinada, Konaseema, Kadapa and Chittoor
x: The shrimp backbone comprises Prakasam, West Godavari, East Godavari, Nellore and Krishna districts.

s: Between the deltas of which rivers does Kolleru Lake, the largest freshwater lake of Andhra Pradesh, lie?
x: Kolleru (about 305 sq km, fed by the Tammileru among others) lies between the Krishna and Godavari deltas.

s: Kolleru Wildlife Sanctuary is associated with which of the following bird species as a breeding ground?
x: Kolleru Wildlife Sanctuary is a breeding ground of the spot-billed pelican and also supports painted storks.

s: What does aquaculture encroachment do to Kolleru Lake?
o: Eliminates all agricultural activity in the surrounding deltas
Turns the lake bed into ponds and fields, causing shrinkage and eutrophication
Converts freshwater into saline water through tidal action
Increases the lake’s depth and improves water circulation
x: Aquaculture ponds and fields have occupied portions of the lake bed, causing the lake to shrink and become eutrophic.

s:
Consider the following statements about Kolleru:
1. The sanctuary limit is the +5 ft contour.
2. It has been a Ramsar site since 2002.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The Kolleru sanctuary boundary is the +5 ft contour, and the lake has been a Ramsar site since 2002.

s: Which one of the following is a freshwater alternative species promoted in Andhra Pradesh aquaculture?
x: GIFT tilapia is listed among the freshwater alternative species. Cobia, lobster and mussel are brackish-water or marine alternatives.

s: Which district produced 9.64 LMT of fish and shrimp worth ₹24,345 crore in 2025-26?
x: West Godavari produced 9.64 LMT of fish and shrimp worth ₹24,345 crore in 2025-26.

s: Which of the following is a feeder stream of Kolleru Lake?
x: Kolleru, between the Krishna and Godavari deltas, is fed by streams such as the Tammileru.

s: About how much area does Kolleru, the largest freshwater lake of Andhra Pradesh, cover?
x: Kolleru, between the Krishna and Godavari deltas, covers about 305 sq km.

s: Which of the following is correct about India's position in world fisheries?
o: The third-largest fish producer and the largest shrimp importer
The largest fish producer and the leading marine-capture country
The second-largest fish producer but a minor inland-capture country
The second-largest fish producer and a leader in inland capture fisheries
x: India is the world's second-largest fish producer (about 8% of world output; some sources say about 9%, FAO SOFIA 2026) and leads the world in inland capture (2.2 MT). It is not the largest producer (B), nor a minor inland-capture country (C).

s: According to the FAO report SOFIA 2026, aquaculture makes up about what share of world aquatic animal output?
x: SOFIA 2026 (FAO) says aquaculture passed 100 million tonnes, about 53% of aquatic animal output.

s: Where is the headquarters of MPEDA, a statutory body under the Ministry of Commerce?
x: MPEDA is headquartered at Kochi.

s: The Juvvaladinne fishing harbour is located in which district?
x: Juvvaladinne is in SPSR Nellore; Uppada is in Kakinada, Nizampatnam in Bapatla and Machilipatnam in Krishna.

s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Phase II fishing harbour projects in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Phase II includes Biyyaputhippa, Kothapatnam, Pudimadaka, Budagatlapalem and Vodarevu. Machilipatnam belongs to the Phase I list.

s: Under which Act are penalties imposed for violation of the Andhra Pradesh fishing-ban provisions?
x: Penalties for the relevant fishing-ban violations are imposed under the AP Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1995.

s: India became the ____ member to accept the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies.
x: India became the 123rd member to accept the Agreement (adopted at MC12 in 2022, in force from September 2025); aquaculture and inland fishing are exempt.

s: Under which Act was APSADA, which licenses aquaculture in Andhra Pradesh, set up?
o: AP State Aquaculture Development Authority Act, 2020
x: The AP State Aquaculture Development Authority Act, 2020 (Act 29 of 2020) set up APSADA.

s: Under the AP State Aquaculture Development Authority Act, 2020, aquaculture zones cover how many coastal districts?
x: Aquaculture zones are set in all 9 coastal districts.

s: Which of the following is a Phase I fishing harbour of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Machilipatnam (Krishna) is a Phase I harbour; Biyyaputhippa, Kothapatnam and Vodarevu are Phase II.

s: Where is the ICAR-CMFRI Regional Centre known for open-sea cage farming in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The ICAR-CMFRI Regional Centre at Visakhapatnam works on open-sea cage farming.

s: Next to which fishing harbour of Andhra Pradesh is the world's first autonomous maritime shipyard (Sagar Defence) coming up?
x: The world's first autonomous maritime shipyard by Sagar Defence is next to Juvvaladinne in SPSR Nellore (March 2026).

s: In which district is the Uppada fishing harbour located?
x: Uppada is a Phase I harbour in Kakinada district; Nizampatnam is in Bapatla.

s: At which WTO Ministerial Conference was the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies adopted?
x: The agreement was adopted at MC12 in 2022 and came into force in September 2025.

s: What is the allocation of the PM-MKSSY sub-scheme (2023-24 to 2026-27), which promotes aquaculture insurance and credit?
x: PM-MKSSY runs from 2023–24 to 2026–27 with an allocation of ₹6,000 crore.

s:
Consider the following statements about the PMMSY subsidy in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The general subsidy is 40 percent.
2. The Government of India bears 24 percent and the State 16 percent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The PMMSY general subsidy is 40 percent, shared as 24 percent by GoI and 16 percent by GoAP.

s: About how many fishermen families received ₹242.86 crore under Matsyakara Sevalo in 2025-26?
x: In 2025-26, ₹242.86 crore went to 1,21,433 families under Matsyakara Sevalo; 1,17,053 is the 2019-20 beneficiary figure.

s: In 2021-22, Andhra Pradesh ranked first in India in the production of which of the following?
x: AP was first in papaya (with oil palm, lime, coconut, cocoa, tomato and chillies); it was second in mango, cashew and sweet orange.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank in India in mango production?
x: AP is second in mango production, not first; it is first in papaya, oil palm, cocoa and lime.

s: Which of the following crop – leading State pairs is wrongly matched?
x: Karnataka leads in silk; Andhra Pradesh is second.

s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh in 2021-22:
1. It ranked first in India in oil palm production.
2. It ranked first in India in cashew production.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: In 2021-22 AP was first in oil palm, but second (not first) in cashew.

s: In which of the following crops does Andhra Pradesh rank second in India?
x: AP is second in mango, cashew and sweet orange; it is first in oil palm, cocoa and papaya.

s: Which district is a cashew hub of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Srikakulam, ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam are the cashew hubs; Anantapur is a banana cluster and Chittoor a mango hub.

s: The banana cluster of Andhra Pradesh is centred on which district?
x: Banana is clustered in Anantapur and Rayalaseema.

s: Konaseema district is a horticulture hub for which crop?
x: Coconut hubs are East Godavari, Konaseema and Srikakulam.

s: Which of the following districts is a mango hub of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Chittoor heads the mango hub districts; Konaseema is coconut, Parvathipuram-Manyam cashew and Anantapur banana.

s: Which is the largest source of net irrigated area in India as a whole?
x: Tube wells lead with 49.34 per cent of India's net irrigated area (2022-23); canals have 22.85 per cent and tanks only 2.82 per cent. Canals lead only in AP.

s: Under the Culturable Command Area classification, how much area does a medium irrigation project cover?
x: A medium project has a CCA of 2,000–10,000 hectares; minor projects are up to 2,000 hectares and major projects exceed 10,000 hectares.

s: Under the Andhra Pradesh classification, minor irrigation refers to an ayacut of up to how many acres?
x: Andhra Pradesh treats an ayacut up to 5,000 acres as minor irrigation.

s: Which provides the largest irrigated area in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Canals irrigate the most area in AP; tube wells lead only at the all-India level.

s: About how many minor irrigation tanks does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: AP's minor irrigation has 38,862 tanks with an ayacut of 25.60 lakh acres.

s: How much irrigation potential had been created in Andhra Pradesh up to December 2024?
x: Total potential created is 106.15 lakh acres; 66.81 is major, 25.60 is minor and 37.63 is the new potential of priority projects.

s: Groundwater accounts for about what share of the gross irrigated area of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Groundwater, through about 19 lakh bore wells, serves about 41% of AP's gross irrigated area; canals remain the main source.

s: Under the culturable command area (CCA) classification, a major irrigation project covers more than how many hectares?
x: Projects above 10,000 ha CCA are major; 2,000–10,000 ha medium; up to 2,000 ha minor.

s: Since which year has the Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project (APMIP) been working?
x: APMIP has run since 2003; in 2024-25 it covered 2.05 lakh acres.

s: Polavaram was declared a national project under which section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
x: Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 declared Polavaram a national project.

s: The Pattiseema lift scheme links which two rivers?
x: Pattiseema lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram right main canal and releases it at Prakasam barrage on the Krishna.

s: The Veligonda (Poola Subbaiah) project, storing water in Nallamala Sagar, serves which district?
x: Veligonda carries Krishna floodwater from the Srisailam foreshore to Prakasam district.

s: How much Krishna floodwater does the Galeru-Nagari Sujala Sravanthi draw from the Srisailam foreshore?
x: Galeru-Nagari Sujala Sravanthi draws 38 TMC of Krishna floodwater for Rayalaseema.

s: The waters of the Vamsadhara project in Srikakulam are shared with which State?
x: The Vamsadhara waters are shared with Odisha.

s: Up to which place has the Handri-Neeva canal, carrying Krishna water, been extended?
x: The Handri-Neeva project carries Krishna water to Rayalaseema, and its canal has been extended to Kuppam.

s: At which barrage is the Godavari water lifted by the Pattiseema scheme released into the Krishna?
x: Pattiseema lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram right main canal and releases it at the Prakasam barrage.

s: Which agency funds the Andhra Pradesh Drought Mitigation Project (APDMP)?
o: The International Fund for Agricultural Development
x: APDMP is funded by the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD). The World Bank is associated with APIIATP.

s: The Gulbenkian Prize associated with Andhra Pradesh agriculture was received by which initiative?
x: Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming received the Gulbenkian Prize in 2024.

s: What is Annadatha Sukhibhava?
x: Annadatha Sukhibhava is the Andhra Pradesh state top-up to PM-KISAN’s ₹6,000 assistance.

s: How many Rythu Seva Kendralu (village one-stop centres, including veterinary services) function in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Rythu Seva Kendralu are 10,606 village one-stop centres in all gram panchayats, including veterinary services.

s: How many agro-climatic zones does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: AP has 6 agro-climatic zones served by ANGRAU research stations.

s: Where is the headquarters of ANGRAU, which serves AP's agro-climatic zones?
x: ANGRAU is headquartered at Lam, Guntur; it shifted from Hyderabad in 2016.

s: Which agency funds the AP Integrated Irrigation and Agriculture Transformation Project (APIIATP)?
x: APIIATP is a World Bank project (US$ 172.2 million, 2018); APDMP is funded by IFAD.

s: What was the earlier name of the Rythu Seva Kendralu of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The 10,606 village one-stop centres were formerly called Rythu Bharosa Kendralu.
